instruction: Could you stream this YouTube video for me using VLC? https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kJQP7kiw5Fk

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Variation of VLC streaming task with a different YouTube video URL (Despacito). Uses the same evaluator pattern (is_vlc_playing with url type). The instruction is paraphrased slightly while maintaining the same task complexity.

llm_judge_reasons: The new metric function includes YouTube video ID extraction logic (extract_youtube_video_id at vlc.py:11-65) which addresses the URL transformation issue identified in the previous judgment

The metric uses multiple matching strategies: (1) Extracts video ID from expected YouTube URL, (2) Searches all URL fields in VLC status.xml for matching video ID, (3) Uses substring matching as fallback if video ID appears anywhere in resolved URLs
The evaluator correctly verifies the instruction requirements: checks VLC is playing (state='playing') and verifies the SPECIFIC YouTube video by comparing video IDs rather than exact URLs
The video ID extraction handles various YouTube URL formats (youtube.com/watch?v=, youtu.be/, embedded URLs) and uses both URL parsing and regex patterns for robustness
The metric collects ALL possible URL/location info from VLC status.xml (lines 138-148) rather than just the first match, increasing chances of finding the video ID
Minor consideration: If VLC's status.xml doesn't preserve any trace of the video ID (unlikely in practice), verification might fail, but the multiple fallback strategies minimize this risk
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding logging to track which URL field in VLC's status.xml contained the matching video ID, to help debug edge cases
Optional: Add a check for video title metadata as an additional verification layer if video ID matching fails (though current logic should be sufficient for most cases)
